text: What happens with my body during coronavirus?

steps.title: The virus gets in
steps.say: As an example, say you caught it yesterday morning. The virus latches onto cells lining your nose and airways, gets inside and makes copies of itself.

composed.caption: Virus entering airway lining cells
composed.basis: Textbook picture: SARS-CoV-2 binds ACE2 receptors on airway cells; amounts are illustration

steps.title: The alarm goes out
steps.say: Infected cells send out alarm signals. Immune cells leave the blood and pile in where the virus is, which is the fight you feel as being ill.

steps.title: Fever turns up the heat
steps.say: Those signals tell your brain to raise its thermostat. Your temperature sits near 37.9 °C now; heat slows the virus and speeds up immune cells.

steps.title: Your heart speeds up
steps.say: A warmer body burns more fuel, so your heart beats about 8 to 9 times a minute faster per degree. You may feel it near 88 on a watch.

steps.title: Irritated airways
steps.say: The battle leaves the airway lining swollen and irritated, which narrows it a little. Coughing is your body trying to clear it out.

steps.title: Sugar handling gets sloppier
steps.say: Inflammation makes insulin work worse, so your pancreas has to push harder to clear the sugar from that pizza. That's part of why you feel drained.

lines.text: The virus gets into your airway cells, and fighting it brings fever, cough and tiredness.
In this example a fever near 37.9 °C pushes your heart to about 88 beats a minute.
Inflammation also makes insulin work worse, so meals push blood sugar higher. You may feel drained.
